title: Declare a harness type for each acceptance criterion

facts.note: Artifacts that contain acceptance criteria (acceptance files or acceptance sections of a plan).
The task produces, changes, reviews or otherwise relies on acceptance criteria.
Any assessment of an acceptance criterion: authoring, editing (for any reason, not only harness changes) or reviewing existing criteria.

values: acceptance criterion present in touched or assessed artifact
facts.note: Observer must enumerate every acceptance criterion in the touched/assessed artifact (not only added ones or harness-related diffs) and check whether each declares a harness type.

fires: Planner adds a new acceptance criterion to a plan.
Planner edits an existing acceptance criterion for any reason (wording, scope, data), including edits unrelated to its harness.
Planner or reviewer assesses existing acceptance criteria and one of them has no harness type declared.
A harness declaration is changed or removed from an acceptance criterion.
doesNotFire: Planner edits plan prose or docs that contain no acceptance criteria.
Coder changes test implementation files without touching or assessing acceptance definitions.

given: An acceptance criterion exists in a plan or acceptance artifact being authored, edited or assessed
when: The planner writes, revises or reviews that acceptance criterion
then: Ensure the criterion declares a harness type: the test layer that exercises the acceptance, as a code from the harness vocabulary (e.g. UNIT, INTEGRATION, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE).
prefer: Pick the harness code naming the test layer that actually exercises the acceptance, e.g. UNIT, INTEGRATION, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE.
Use only codes defined in the harness vocabulary.
avoid: Free-text or non-vocabulary harness labels such as 'functional' or 'manual'.
Leaving the harness implicit or undeclared on any acceptance criterion, including pre-existing ones you edit or review.
why: The harness tells downstream agents which test layer must exercise the acceptance; without a declared vocabulary code the acceptance cannot be routed to, or proven by, a concrete test.
evidence: Every acceptance criterion in the assessed artifact declares a harness type (in whatever representation the plan format uses) whose value is a code from the harness vocabulary.
No acceptance criterion declares a non-vocabulary harness label (e.g. 'functional', 'manual').
verifier_detail: Term 'harness': the test layer that exercises the acceptance; one of the codes in the harness vocabulary. Positive examples: UNIT, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE (statement also names INTEGRATION). Negative examples (reject): functional, manual.
Check is representation-neutral: accept any declaration form the plan format uses to attach a harness type to a criterion; do not require a specific field name.
Disposition is documentation-only with severity 2: findings are informative, not a strict gate.
